group: Ball hits another player or an outside influence

Other player on the green is present but not interacting with the ball.

questions.title: What Happens If Your Ball Hits Someone On The Green?
questions.question: You putt your ball on the green and it accidentally hits another player who is also on the green. What do you need to do next?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it stopped
Take your putt again with no penalty
Add a penalty stroke and keep playing
Move your ball to the nearest spot

questions.explanation: If your ball hits another player on the green, you get to take your putt again. You don’t get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth, grassy area where you try to putt the ball into the hole.
A soft shot on the green to roll the ball toward the hole.

questions.teachingTip: Ask children to pretend to putt and imagine their ball hits a friend’s shoe on the green. Talk about why the ball needs to be replayed instead of left where it stopped.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they have to play from where the ball ends up, like in most places on the course.
They may think they get a penalty even if it wasn't on purpose.

questions.title: Ball Hits Another Player On The Green – What Now?
questions.question: You putt from the green and your ball accidentally strikes another player who is also on the green. What must you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it comes to rest
Replay the stroke with no penalty
Add a penalty stroke and play on
Move your ball to the nearest spot

questions.explanation: If your ball accidentally hits another player on the putting green, you must replay the stroke and there is no penalty.
